newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golds weigh on Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Golds weigh on Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian stock market edged just lower at the open on Friday with a gold-weakened resources sector weighing on the broader market.
The All Ordinaries index slipped just 0.9 points to 2,742.0.

The gold sector benchmark lost over four percent after the bullion price hit a 12 year low after news that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) had sold 167 tonnes of its gold reserves over the past six months.

"That is about six straight days down on the gold price now and that's a fair whack from almost US$340 down to US$324. People are getting very nervous about it no matter what happens now," said dealer at Reynolds and Co, Peter Struk.
Single largest component in the sector, Normandy Mining, opened over eight percent lower at A$1.333 (US$1.00) before regaining some ground.
Normandy accounts for nearly 20 percent of the sector benchmark, the gold index, which hit its lowest level in over four years.

Among others, Newcrest Mining was over three percent lower at A$3.30, while Plutonic Resources was 5.5 percent down at A$3.95. Acacia Resources was at A$1.63, down three percent, as was Emperor Mines and Sons of Gwalia at A$1.60 and A$4.75 respectively. Great Central Mines lost nearly four percent to A$2.42.
In the broader market, moves in the leaders were modest, with the tone outside the gold sector mildly positive.
"The rest of it looks good with new highs in London, the Dow and in the S&P500," Reynold's Struk said, although he suspected some pre-U.S. holiday selling may emerge late in the day.
"It may get knocked down this afternoon with New York closed tonight."
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of more than two to one, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
